items.en: to put your foot in it; to blunder

example.es: Metí la pata cuando le pregunté por su ex.
example.en: I put my foot in it when I asked about her ex.

items.en: to pull someone's leg; to tease

example.es: No te creo, me estás tomando el pelo.
example.en: I don't believe you, you're pulling my leg.

items.en: to have your head in the clouds; to daydream

example.es: Hoy estás en las nubes, ¿qué te pasa?
example.en: You're daydreaming today, what's up with you?

items.en: to be a piece of cake; to be very easy

example.es: El examen fue pan comido.
example.en: The exam was a piece of cake.

items.en: to rain cats and dogs; to pour

example.es: Lleva paraguas, está lloviendo a cántaros.
example.en: Take an umbrella, it's pouring.

items.es: costar un ojo de la cara
items.en: to cost an arm and a leg
items.literal: to cost an eye from your face

example.es: Ese coche me costó un ojo de la cara.
example.en: That car cost me an arm and a leg.

items.en: to talk nonstop; to be a chatterbox
items.literal: to talk even through your elbows

example.es: Mi tía habla hasta por los codos.
example.en: My aunt never stops talking.

items.es: no tener pelos en la lengua
items.en: to speak your mind; to not mince words
items.literal: to have no hairs on your tongue

example.es: Ana no tiene pelos en la lengua: siempre dice lo que piensa.
example.en: Ana doesn't mince words: she always says what she thinks.

items.en: to keep an eye on; to have a look at

example.es: ¿Le puedes echar un ojo a mi maleta?
example.en: Can you keep an eye on my suitcase?

items.en: to get to the point

example.es: No tengo mucho tiempo, vamos al grano.
example.en: I don't have much time, let's get to the point.

items.en: to hit the nail on the head; to get it exactly right

example.es: Con ese regalo diste en el clavo.
example.en: You got it exactly right with that gift.

items.en: to get your act together; to get moving

example.es: Si quieres aprobar, ponte las pilas.
example.en: If you want to pass, get your act together.

items.es: tirar la casa por la ventana
items.en: to splash out; to spare no expense
items.literal: to throw the house out the window

example.es: Para la boda tiraron la casa por la ventana.
example.en: They spared no expense for the wedding.

items.en: to add fuel to the fire
items.literal: to throw firewood on the fire

example.es: No eches leña al fuego, ya están bastante enojados.
example.en: Don't add fuel to the fire, they're angry enough already.

items.en: to overcomplicate things; to look for problems where there are none
items.literal: to look for three feet on the cat

example.es: Es muy sencillo, no le busques tres pies al gato.
example.en: It's very simple, don't overcomplicate it.

items.en: to rip someone off; to pass off something inferior
items.literal: to give cat instead of hare

example.es: Revisa bien el reloj, que no te den gato por liebre.
example.en: Check the watch carefully so they don't rip you off.

items.en: to be inseparable; to be very close

example.es: Pedro y Luis son uña y carne desde la escuela.
example.en: Pedro and Luis have been inseparable since school.

items.es: estar entre la espada y la pared
items.en: to be between a rock and a hard place
items.literal: to be between the sword and the wall

example.es: Con esa decisión me pusiste entre la espada y la pared.
example.en: With that decision you put me between a rock and a hard place.

items.en: to drive someone crazy; to infuriate

example.es: Ese ruido me saca de quicio.
example.en: That noise drives me crazy.

items.es: en un abrir y cerrar de ojos
items.en: in the blink of an eye
items.literal: in an opening and closing of eyes

example.es: Lo hizo en un abrir y cerrar de ojos.
example.en: He did it in the blink of an eye.

items.en: to cheat on someone

example.es: Se enteró de que su novio le ponía los cuernos.
example.en: She found out her boyfriend was cheating on her.

items.en: to play dumb; to pretend not to notice
items.literal: to make yourself the crazy one

example.es: Le pregunté por el dinero y se hizo el loco.
example.en: I asked him about the money and he played dumb.

items.en: to pester; to be a nuisance

example.es: Los niños me dieron la lata toda la tarde.
example.en: The kids pestered me all afternoon.

items.en: to not care at all; to not give a hoot

example.es: Lo que digan los demás me importa un comino.
example.en: I couldn't care less what others say.

items.en: to be stunned; to be speechless
items.literal: to be left made of stone

example.es: Cuando vi el precio me quedé de piedra.
example.en: When I saw the price I was stunned.

items.es: tener la sartén por el mango
items.en: to be in control; to call the shots
items.literal: to hold the frying pan by the handle

example.es: En esta empresa, ella tiene la sartén por el mango.
example.en: In this company, she calls the shots.

items.en: to rest on your laurels
items.literal: to fall asleep on the laurels

example.es: Ganaron una vez y se durmieron en los laureles.
example.en: They won once and rested on their laurels.

items.en: to sleep on it
items.literal: to consult it with the pillow

example.es: No decidas ahora, consúltalo con la almohada.
example.en: Don't decide now, sleep on it.

items.en: to take the blame (for others); to carry the can
items.literal: to pay for the broken plates

example.es: Él hizo el desastre y yo pagué los platos rotos.
example.en: He made the mess and I took the blame.

items.en: to turn a blind eye

example.es: El profesor hizo la vista gorda con el retraso.
example.en: The teacher turned a blind eye to the lateness.

items.es: ser un cero a la izquierda
items.en: to be a nobody; to count for nothing
items.literal: to be a zero on the left

example.es: En las reuniones me siento un cero a la izquierda.
example.en: In meetings I feel like I count for nothing.

items.en: to be always on duty; to never give up
items.literal: to be at the foot of the cannon

example.es: Mi abuela, a sus noventa años, sigue al pie del cañón.
example.en: My grandmother, at ninety, is still going strong.

items.en: to fight like cats and dogs
items.literal: to get along like dog and cat

example.es: Mis hermanos se llevan como perro y gato.
example.en: My brothers fight like cats and dogs.

items.en: to be in your element

example.es: En la cocina, mi padre está en su salsa.
example.en: In the kitchen, my father is in his element.

items.en: all of a sudden; out of the blue
items.literal: from good ones to first ones

example.es: De buenas a primeras, decidió mudarse a Canadá.
example.en: Out of the blue, he decided to move to Canada.

items.en: to make your mouth water
items.literal: for your mouth to turn to water

example.es: Con ese olor se me hace agua la boca.
example.en: That smell makes my mouth water.

items.en: to be fast asleep; to be done for

example.es: Si mi jefe se entera, estoy frito.
example.en: If my boss finds out, I'm done for.

items.en: to be a nice, easygoing person

example.es: Tu primo es muy buena onda.
example.en: Your cousin is really nice.

note.en: Very common in Mexico. Mala onda is the opposite: ¡Qué mala onda! = That's not cool!

items.en: oh well; nothing can be done

example.es: Se acabaron los boletos. Ni modo, vamos mañana.
example.en: The tickets sold out. Oh well, let's go tomorrow.

items.en: to give it your all; to try hard

example.es: ¡Échale ganas al examen!
example.en: Give the exam your all!

items.en: really? no way!

example.es: ¿A poco ya terminaste?
example.en: No way, you're already done?

items.en: watch out!; careful!

example.es: ¡Aguas con el perro, que muerde!
example.en: Watch out for the dog, it bites!

items.en: to humor someone; to pretend to listen

example.es: No me estás escuchando, me estás dando el avión.
example.en: You're not listening, you're just humoring me.

items.en: to be fed up
items.literal: to be up to the cap

example.es: Estoy hasta el gorro de tanto tráfico.
example.en: I'm fed up with all this traffic.

items.en: to be furious; to be boiling mad
items.literal: to be like water for chocolate (about to boil)

example.es: Después de la discusión, estaba como agua para chocolate.
example.en: After the argument, she was boiling mad.

note.en: Hot chocolate is made with water brought nearly to the boil, hence the image (and the novel's title).

items.en: to skip school; to play hooky

example.es: Ayer nos fuimos de pinta al cine.
example.en: Yesterday we skipped school and went to the movies.

note.en: Spain says hacer novillos or hacer pellas.

items.en: to be hungover

example.es: No me hables fuerte, estoy crudo.
example.en: Don't talk loudly, I'm hungover.

note.en: La cruda is a hangover in Mexico; Spain says tener resaca.

items.en: how embarrassing!

example.es: Me caí enfrente de todos. ¡Qué oso!
example.en: I fell in front of everyone. How embarrassing!

items.en: to goof around; to make a racket

example.es: Los niños estuvieron echando relajo toda la clase.
example.en: The kids were goofing around the whole class.

items.en: great; awesome

example.es: La fiesta estuvo a todo dar.
example.en: The party was awesome.

items.en: right away; in a flash

example.es: Voy a la tienda de volada y regreso.
example.en: I'll pop to the store and be right back.

items.en: a lot; loads

example.es: Te quiero un chorro.
example.en: I love you loads.

items.en: really? for real?

example.es: ¿Neta te vas a vivir a España?
example.en: For real, you're moving to Spain?

note.en: La neta = the honest truth: La neta, no me gustó.

items.en: to be posh; to be stuck-up

example.es: Esa escuela es muy fresa.
example.en: That school is really posh.

items.en: to be broke

example.es: No puedo salir, estoy bruja hasta la quincena.
example.en: I can't go out, I'm broke until payday.

items.en: to be hard (for someone)

example.es: Me cuesta trabajo levantarme temprano.
example.en: I find it hard to get up early.

note.en: Also heard in Spain, where costar (alone) is more common: me cuesta levantarme.

items.en: no problem

example.es: ¿Te ayudo? — No hay bronca, yo puedo.
example.en: Shall I help you? — No problem, I can do it.

items.en: to be nuts; to be crazy

example.es: Tu vecino está como una cabra.
example.en: Your neighbor is nuts.

items.en: to be amazing (or the limit)

example.es: Este grupo es la leche, me encanta.
example.en: This band is amazing, I love it.

note.en: Tone decides: ¡Eres la leche! can be praise or exasperation.

items.en: to be exhausted; to be worn out

example.es: Después del viaje estoy hecho polvo.
example.en: After the trip I'm worn out.

items.en: to be totally amazed

example.es: Cuando vi el concierto flipé en colores.
example.en: When I saw the concert I was blown away.

items.en: to be in on it; to be in the know

example.es: No me cuentes nada, que no estoy en el ajo.
example.en: Don't tell me anything, I'm not in on it.

items.en: to have a nasty temper; to be mean

example.es: Ten cuidado con el jefe, tiene muy mala leche.
example.en: Be careful with the boss, he has a nasty temper.

items.en: to stuff yourself (with food)

example.es: En Navidad nos pusimos morados de turrón.
example.en: At Christmas we stuffed ourselves with nougat.

items.en: to be a drag; to be boring

example.es: La película fue un rollo.
example.en: The movie was a drag.

note.en: ¡Qué buen rollo! means 'what good vibes!'.

items.en: to be in a bad mood

example.es: Hoy Juan está de mala uva.
example.en: Juan is in a bad mood today.

items.en: to not sleep a wink

example.es: Con el calor no pegué ojo en toda la noche.
example.en: With the heat I didn't sleep a wink all night.

items.en: to be broke
items.literal: to be without a white (an old coin)

example.es: A final de mes siempre estoy sin blanca.
example.en: At the end of the month I'm always broke.

items.en: to take a long weekend (bridging a holiday)

example.es: El jueves es fiesta, así que hacemos puente.
example.en: Thursday is a holiday, so we're taking Friday off too.

items.en: to pretend not to understand

example.es: Le pedí que pagara y se hizo el sueco.
example.en: I asked him to pay and he pretended not to understand.

items.en: to be really cool

example.es: Tu chaqueta mola mazo.
example.en: Your jacket is really cool.

note.en: Youthful slang from Spain; mazo means 'a lot'.

items.en: to be broke; to be clueless

example.es: Me pagan el lunes; hasta entonces estoy a dos velas.
example.en: I get paid on Monday; until then I'm broke.

items.en: to have connections (to get a job or favor)

example.es: Consiguió el trabajo porque tiene enchufe.
example.en: He got the job because he has connections.

items.en: to be a suck-up; to be a brown-noser

example.es: No seas pelota con el profe.
example.en: Don't suck up to the teacher.

items.en: to be fed up
items.literal: to be up to the nostrils

example.es: Estoy hasta las narices de este ruido.
example.en: I'm fed up with this noise.

items.es: no ver tres en un burro
items.en: to be as blind as a bat
items.literal: to not see three on a donkey

example.es: Sin gafas no veo tres en un burro.
example.en: Without glasses I'm as blind as a bat.

items.en: to be tactful; to handle people well

example.es: Para ese puesto hace falta tener mano izquierda.
example.en: That position requires tact.

items.en: to turn out a disappointment

example.es: El nuevo fichaje salió rana.
example.en: The new signing turned out to be a disappointment.

items.en: to go out for tapas

example.es: Los viernes vamos de tapas por el centro.
example.en: On Fridays we go out for tapas downtown.

items.en: to be a (foreign) tourist

example.es: En verano la playa se llena de guiris.
example.en: In summer the beach fills up with tourists.

note.en: Informal Spain slang for foreigners, usually northern European tourists; mildly teasing.

items.en: better late than never
items.literal: later is worth more than never

example.es: Llegaste tarde, pero más vale tarde que nunca.
example.en: You arrived late, but better late than never.

items.es: no hay mal que por bien no venga
items.en: every cloud has a silver lining
items.literal: there is no bad that doesn't come for good

example.es: Perdí el tren, pero conocí a mi esposa. No hay mal que por bien no venga.
example.en: I missed the train, but I met my wife. Every cloud has a silver lining.

items.es: en boca cerrada no entran moscas
items.en: silence is golden; better to keep quiet
items.literal: flies don't get into a closed mouth

example.es: No digas nada; en boca cerrada no entran moscas.
example.en: Don't say anything; better to keep quiet.

items.es: camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente
items.en: you snooze, you lose
items.literal: the shrimp that falls asleep is carried away by the current

example.es: Hay que comprar las entradas ya: camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente.
example.en: We need to buy the tickets now: you snooze, you lose.

items.es: dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres
items.en: you are the company you keep
items.literal: tell me who you walk with and I'll tell you who you are

example.es: Cuidado con esos amigos: dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres.
example.en: Careful with those friends: you are the company you keep.

items.en: keep smiling through hard times
items.literal: to bad weather, a good face

example.es: Se canceló el vuelo, pero al mal tiempo, buena cara.
example.en: The flight was canceled, but let's keep smiling.

items.es: ojos que no ven, corazón que no siente
items.en: out of sight, out of mind; what you don't know won't hurt you
items.literal: eyes that don't see, heart that doesn't feel

example.es: No le cuentes lo del coche; ojos que no ven, corazón que no siente.
example.en: Don't tell him about the car; what he doesn't know won't hurt him.

items.es: del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho
items.en: easier said than done
items.literal: from the said to the done there's a long stretch

example.es: Quiere correr un maratón, pero del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho.
example.en: He wants to run a marathon, but that's easier said than done.

items.es: a quien madruga, Dios le ayuda
items.en: the early bird catches the worm
items.literal: God helps the one who gets up early

example.es: Me levanté a las seis y conseguí las mejores entradas. A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda.
example.en: I got up at six and got the best tickets. The early bird catches the worm.

items.en: to each their own

example.es: A él le gustan los trenes y a ella los sellos: cada loco con su tema.
example.en: He likes trains and she likes stamps: to each their own.

items.es: a otro perro con ese hueso
items.en: tell that to someone else; I'm not buying it
items.literal: to another dog with that bone

example.es: ¿Que el perro se comió tu tarea? A otro perro con ese hueso.
example.en: The dog ate your homework? I'm not buying it.

items.en: like father, like son
items.literal: from such a stick, such a splinter

example.es: Juega al fútbol igual que su padre. De tal palo, tal astilla.
example.en: He plays soccer just like his father. Like father, like son.

items.es: más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando
items.en: a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
items.literal: a bird in hand is worth more than a hundred flying

example.es: Acepta esa oferta; más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando.
example.en: Take that offer; a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

items.es: no es oro todo lo que reluce
items.en: all that glitters is not gold
items.literal: not everything that shines is gold

example.es: El trabajo parece perfecto, pero no es oro todo lo que reluce.
example.en: The job looks perfect, but all that glitters is not gold.

items.en: his bark is worse than his bite
items.literal: a dog that barks doesn't bite

example.es: El jefe grita mucho, pero perro que ladra no muerde.
example.en: The boss shouts a lot, but his bark is worse than his bite.

items.es: poco a poco se va lejos
items.en: slow and steady wins the race
items.literal: little by little you go far

example.es: No te desanimes con el español; poco a poco se va lejos.
example.en: Don't get discouraged with Spanish; slow and steady wins the race.

items.en: to be in a good mood

example.es: Pídeselo ahora, que está de buenas.
example.en: Ask him now, he's in a good mood.

items.en: to have bad luck

example.es: ¡Qué mala pata! Se me pinchó la rueda.
example.en: What bad luck! I got a flat tire.

items.en: to be all confused
items.literal: to be turned into a mess

example.es: Con tantos horarios estoy hecho un lío.
example.en: With so many schedules I'm all confused.

items.en: to change your mindset

example.es: Ahora que eres jefe, tienes que cambiar el chip.
example.en: Now that you're the boss, you need to change your mindset.

items.en: to have a blast

example.es: En la fiesta nos lo pasamos bomba.
example.en: We had a blast at the party.

note.en: Mexico would say la pasamos súper bien or estuvo padrísimo.

items.en: no worries; it's fine

example.es: ¿Te pisé? — No pasa nada.
example.en: Did I step on you? — No worries.

items.en: I hope so!; if only!

example.es: ¿Crees que mañana haga sol? — ¡Ojalá!
example.en: Do you think it'll be sunny tomorrow? — I hope so!

note.en: Ojalá is followed by the subjunctive: ojalá que llueva.

items.en: enjoy your meal!

example.es: Aquí tienen sus platos. ¡Buen provecho!
example.en: Here are your dishes. Enjoy your meal!

note.en: In Mexico it's polite to say provecho to people eating as you pass; Spain more often says ¡que aproveche!

items.en: to miss (someone or something)

example.es: Te echo mucho de menos.
example.en: I miss you a lot.

note.en: Mexico says extrañar: te extraño mucho.

items.en: to hurry up

example.es: ¡Date prisa, que perdemos el tren!
example.en: Hurry up, we'll miss the train!

note.en: Mexico says apurarse: ¡apúrate!

items.en: to feel like (doing something)

example.es: Tengo ganas de ir a la playa.
example.en: I feel like going to the beach.

items.en: to not matter; to be all the same

example.es: ¿Pizza o tacos? — Me da igual.
example.en: Pizza or tacos? — I don't mind.

items.en: to be worth it

example.es: El viaje fue largo, pero valió la pena.
example.en: The trip was long, but it was worth it.

items.en: to realize

example.es: No me di cuenta de la hora.
example.en: I didn't realize what time it was.

note.en: Realizar is a false friend: it means to carry out, not to realize.

items.en: to pay attention to; to listen to (advice)

example.es: Nunca me haces caso.
example.en: You never listen to me.

items.en: to agree

example.es: Estoy de acuerdo contigo.
example.en: I agree with you.

items.en: to take into account; to bear in mind

example.es: Ten en cuenta que cierran a las ocho.
example.en: Bear in mind that they close at eight.

items.en: to get along well

example.es: Me llevo muy bien con mis compañeros.
example.en: I get along really well with my coworkers.

items.en: to like (a person); to get a good impression of

example.es: Tu novio me cae muy bien.
example.en: I really like your boyfriend.

note.en: Works like gustar: the person liked is the subject. Caer mal = to dislike.

items.es: sobre gustos no hay nada escrito
items.en: there's no accounting for taste
items.literal: about tastes there is nothing written

example.es: A él le encanta la piña en la pizza; sobre gustos no hay nada escrito.
example.en: He loves pineapple on pizza; there's no accounting for taste.

items.en: to be hungry

example.es: Tengo mucha hambre; ¿comemos ya?
example.en: I'm really hungry; shall we eat now?

note.en: Spanish "has" hunger, thirst (sed), sleepiness (sueño), cold (frío) and heat (calor).

items.en: to be sleepy

example.es: Los niños tienen sueño; vamos a casa.
example.en: The kids are sleepy; let's go home.

items.en: to be in a hurry

example.es: Perdona, no puedo hablar: tengo prisa.
example.en: Sorry, I can't talk: I'm in a hurry.

items.en: to go for a walk

example.es: Después de comer damos un paseo por el parque.
example.en: After lunch we go for a walk in the park.

items.en: to be needed

example.es: No hace falta que vengas; ya lo hago yo.
example.en: There's no need for you to come; I'll do it.

items.en: to be in fashion; to be trendy

example.es: Ese restaurante está de moda este año.
example.en: That restaurant is trendy this year.

items.en: to blush

example.es: Se puso rojo cuando ella le sonrió.
example.en: He blushed when she smiled at him.

items.en: to beat around the bush; to go off on a tangent
items.literal: to go off along the branches

example.es: No te vayas por las ramas y dime qué pasó.
example.en: Don't beat around the bush; tell me what happened.

items.es: matar dos pájaros de un tiro
items.en: to kill two birds with one stone
items.literal: to kill two birds with one shot

example.es: Voy al banco y al súper a la vez: mato dos pájaros de un tiro.
example.en: I'll go to the bank and the supermarket together: two birds with one stone.

items.es: no tener ni pies ni cabeza
items.en: to make no sense at all
items.literal: to have neither feet nor head

example.es: Esa historia no tiene ni pies ni cabeza.
example.en: That story makes no sense at all.

items.es: ser la gota que colma el vaso
items.en: to be the last straw
items.literal: to be the drop that fills the glass to the brim

example.es: Llegó tarde otra vez, y eso fue la gota que colmó el vaso.
example.en: He was late again, and that was the last straw.

note.en: In Mexico it is often la gota que derramó el vaso: the drop that spilled the glass.

items.es: no dar el brazo a torcer
items.en: to refuse to give in; to stand your ground
items.literal: not to let your arm be twisted

example.es: Sabe que no tiene razón, pero no da el brazo a torcer.
example.en: He knows he's wrong, but he won't back down.

items.es: a la tercera va la vencida
items.en: third time lucky
items.literal: on the third, the beaten one goes

example.es: Ya lo intenté dos veces; a la tercera va la vencida.
example.en: I've already tried twice; third time's the charm.

items.es: ahogarse en un vaso de agua
items.en: to make a mountain out of a molehill
items.literal: to drown in a glass of water

example.es: No te ahogues en un vaso de agua: tiene arreglo.
example.en: Don't make a mountain out of a molehill: it can be fixed.

items.es: estar con el agua al cuello
items.en: to be up to your neck (in trouble or debt)
items.literal: to be with the water up to the neck

example.es: Con tantas deudas, están con el agua al cuello.
example.en: With so many debts, they're up to their necks.

items.es: a caballo regalado no se le mira el diente
items.en: don't look a gift horse in the mouth
items.literal: you don't look at the teeth of a gifted horse

example.es: La bici es vieja, pero a caballo regalado no se le mira el diente.
example.en: The bike is old, but don't look a gift horse in the mouth.

items.en: to tread carefully

example.es: Con este cliente hay que andar con pies de plomo.
example.en: With this client you have to tread carefully.

items.en: to throw something back in someone's face; to reproach

example.es: Siempre me echa en cara que llegué tarde a su boda.
example.en: She always throws it in my face that I was late to her wedding.

items.en: to make a killing; to cash in

example.es: Con el calor, los vendedores de helados hicieron su agosto.
example.en: With the heat, the ice-cream sellers made a killing.

note.en: August was harvest time, when farmers earned their year's money.

items.es: tener la mosca detrás de la oreja
items.en: to be suspicious; to smell a rat
items.literal: to have the fly behind the ear

example.es: Desde que vi el mensaje, tengo la mosca detrás de la oreja.
example.en: Ever since I saw the message, I've smelled a rat.

items.en: to get it; to catch on

example.es: Al principio no entendía el juego, pero ya le agarré la onda.
example.en: At first I didn't get the game, but now I've caught on.

items.en: to be in the middle of nowhere; to be miles away
items.literal: to be at the fifth pine

example.es: Su casa está en el quinto pino; tardamos una hora en llegar.
example.en: Their house is miles away; it took us an hour to get there.

items.en: too little, too late

example.es: ¿Ahora me pides perdón? A buenas horas, mangas verdes.
example.en: Now you apologize? Too little, too late.

note.en: The green sleeves were the uniforms of a medieval rural police that always arrived after the crime.

items.en: to pluck up courage; to grit your teeth
items.literal: to make a heart out of guts

example.es: Hice de tripas corazón y le dije la verdad.
example.en: I plucked up my courage and told him the truth.

items.en: to have it both ways; to play it safe
items.literal: to swim and keep an eye on your clothes

example.es: Quiere apoyar el proyecto sin arriesgar nada: nadar y guardar la ropa.
example.en: He wants to back the project without risking anything: having it both ways.

items.es: cría cuervos y te sacarán los ojos
items.en: raise crows and they'll peck your eyes out (ingratitude)
items.literal: raise crows and they will take out your eyes

example.es: Lo ayudé en todo y ahora me critica. Cría cuervos…
example.en: I helped him with everything and now he criticizes me. Raise crows…

items.es: vender la piel del oso antes de cazarlo
items.en: to count your chickens before they hatch
items.literal: to sell the bear's skin before hunting it

example.es: Todavía no te han contratado; no vendas la piel del oso antes de cazarlo.
example.en: They haven't hired you yet; don't count your chickens before they hatch.

items.es: a falta de pan, buenas son tortas
items.en: beggars can't be choosers
items.literal: for lack of bread, cakes are good

example.es: No había taxis, así que tomamos el metro: a falta de pan, buenas son tortas.
example.en: There were no taxis, so we took the metro: beggars can't be choosers.

items.en: to be a different matter; another kettle of fish
items.literal: to be flour from another sack

example.es: El sueldo está bien; el horario es harina de otro costal.
example.en: The salary is fine; the hours are another matter.

items.en: to come out on top; to win the day
items.literal: to take the cat to the water

example.es: Después de mucho discutir, ella se llevó el gato al agua.
example.en: After a long argument, she came out on top.

items.en: to give someone a piece of your mind

example.es: Llegó tarde otra vez y su jefa le cantó las cuarenta.
example.en: He was late again and his boss gave him a piece of her mind.

note.en: From the card game tute, where announcing "las cuarenta" wins forty points.

items.en: to grope in the dark; to act blindly

example.es: Sin datos, el gobierno está dando palos de ciego.
example.en: Without data, the government is groping in the dark.

items.en: to throw up your hands in horror (often hypocritically)

example.es: Todos se rasgan las vestiduras, pero nadie hace nada.
example.en: Everyone throws up their hands in horror, but nobody does anything.
